item.title: Trump proposes new retirement plan for private-sector workers
item.description: President Donald Trump proposes a $1,000 federal retirement match for private-sector workers, expanding access to savings plans ahead of 2026 midterms.

item.title: Trump tells tech companies to build power plants for data centers
item.description: President Trump announced tech companies must build their own power plants for data centers to reduce electricity costs and protect consumers from rising bills.

item.title: Wisconsin construction panel talks safety, labor shortages
item.description: Wisconsin construction leaders discuss OSHA staffing, safety training and growing apprentice ranks as megaprojects increase demand for skilled trades.

item.title: Twin Cities residents see 3.7% increase in pay
item.description: Twin Cities private industry workers saw a 3.7% wage increase in 2025, ranking third among 15 US metros for total compensation growth, per BLS data.

item.title: Spring Parade of Homes coming to Rochester
item.description: Housing First Minnesota’s Spring Parade of Homes is expanding into Rochester this year.

item.title: Greiner selected for repurposing Yamasaki Building
item.description: About three months after buying the building, CDT Realty Corporation has selected Greiner Construction as the general contractor for the conversion of the Yamasaki Building.

item.title: Hendrickson to become Adolfson & Peterson’s new CEO in June
item.description: Adolfson & Peterson Construction appoints COO Brad Hendrickson as CEO effective June 1, succeeding Jeff Hansen who retires after leading since 2017.

item.title: U.S. looks to raise tariffs to 15% for some countries
item.description: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer says some tariffs could rise to 15% while maintaining trade deals, targeting unfair practices and industrial overcapacity.

item.title: Growing popularity brings narrower window for tax credit
item.description: Minnesota Housing’s State Housing Tax Credit program exhausted $9.9M in two hours as developers and donors rushed to fund income-restricted housing projects.

item.title: Plymouth approves TIF for $62M redevelopment
item.description: Plymouth approves a $4.76M TIF plan for a $62M redevelopment of Plymouth Plaza, adding 195 apartments, new commercial space and affordable housing.
